This is goal g-33a7a4ae, round 2 (fix round; round 1 was audit-only and already merged as docs/state/silent-failures.md; several fix batches already merged for other files, including the near-identical process-kill pattern in tools/ui-check.mjs). Read that doc's methodology section first (top of file) and the per-file section for tools/managers/visual-qa/screenshots.mjs (search for '### tools/managers/visual-qa/screenshots.mjs' - it lists exact line numbers and the catch form found there: try-catch-no-binding, dot-catch-arrow, or dot-catch-noop-expr).

IMPORTANT - this file is sensitive: three flagged catches (re-find them by content, not by exact line number) wrap process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL') calls used to kill dev-server/browser child processes this tool started - `killLive`'s loop, the `kill(signal)` helper's process.kill-then-child.kill fallback, and `stop()`'s process.kill. The expected case there is the process already being gone (ESRCH) - `kill` on an already-dead pid throws, and that's normal, not a bug. Your fix must: (a) keep every kill call itself completely unchanged (same target, same signal, same timing), (b) keep the cleanup non-blocking (never add a throw that would stop the rest of cleanup), (c) narrow the catch to stay silent for the expected ESRCH case and log anything else unexpected via console.error.

The other five flagged catches are NOT process-kill related - they are a waitForSelector fallback inside a generated/inline browser-script context, a best-effort file-handle close during error cleanup, a log-tail read, a readLedger fallback, and similar best-effort reads. Treat those as ordinary best-effort fallbacks per the rules below.

For EACH flagged line in tools/managers/visual-qa/screenshots.mjs only (do not touch any other file, do not touch anything beyond the flagged catch blocks):

1. Read the surrounding function to understand what the catch is actually guarding against and what happens today when it swallows silently (what does the function return/do next).
2. Decide, from the real code, whether this catch is:
   (a) An EXPECTED/benign condition - the process-already-gone case described above for the three kill sites, a selector that may legitimately not appear, a best-effort file write/close, a log file or ledger that may not exist. For these, keep the swallow (do not change control flow or add noisy logging for the expected path), but narrow to the specific expected error code where one exists (ESRCH for kill calls, ENOENT for missing files) and add minimal visibility (see point 3) for anything else unexpected - same return value, same behavior, just visible.
   (b) A genuinely UNEXPECTED-error catch with no narrower expected case. Add minimal visibility only: a one-line log. This file has no existing logger/journal convention of its own - use `console.error('[tools/managers/visual-qa/screenshots.mjs] <short context naming the function/operation>:', error?.message ?? error)`. Do NOT add a throw, do NOT change the function's return value or control flow, do NOT change what happens next.
3. If a catch binds no error variable, add a REAL binding and actually reference it in a console.error call - do not just rename-and-ignore a binding (including via a `void error;` no-op - if a site should truly stay silent, say so in your summary and explain why rather than adding an unused binding).

Do not refactor anything beyond the flagged catch blocks. Do not reformat unrelated code. Do not rename functions or change exports. Preserve every existing behavior path exactly except for the narrowing/visibility described above.

Your workspace does not include the test suite, so you cannot run it yourself - the orchestrator runs the real full suite against your output after integration, and will also get this reviewed via the claude CLI before merge given the sensitivity (process-kill), and will send back any issue as a follow-up. List, in your final summary, which of the 8 flagged lines you touched, case (a) vs (b), with one line each, and confirm all three kill() calls are unchanged.
